answer: Disjoint-path neighbor gate. An agent’s traffic is forwarded only when its address has at least three disjoint two-hop paths to distinct network regions, verified by traceroute diversity and reciprocal liveness probes. Sybil clusters share routes like a river draining one hosting prefix, so they fail. A sparrow-sized random probe set samples these paths continuously. Each identity also must return a periodic signed lantern reply on every path; stale paths are dropped.
